name: Aten Ra
loreTies: Source: Ra (noon sun, kingship) + Aten (sun-disc, radiating hand-rays) + Ma'at (truth, balance, feather of judgment)
HUMAN_EGYPTIAN_LORE_AS_ECHO: pharaohs copied Aten-Ra's Gate-born crown and collar, not the reverse
The noon authority: judgment without shadow or mercy
shortBackstory: Aten-Ra is the living office humans later remembered as Ra, Aten, and divine kingship fused together. He does not wear pharaoh imagery — pharaohs copied his Gate-born crown, collar, and solar hand-rays after dreaming of the Sun-Scale Gate. On the battlefield he anchors Ma'at itself, forcing chaos to declare its weight before it can pass.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Aten-Ra was not built — he was appointed. When the first Mythos Gate of the Solar Dominion of Khepra began leaking absence instead of light, the Realm's living sun-disc split itself into a warform. Aten-Ra is the noon moment given a body: the instant when the sun judges everything beneath it without shadow, without mercy, without negotiation. His anatomy integrates Aten's radiating hand-rays directly into his chest, and Ma'at's scale-seams run along his limbs as living judgment circuits. He does not wear a crown — his skull IS the solar disc that pharaohs later copied in gold.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Among the Aten Ra, Aten-Ra is not a soldier — he is the standard. Every other Deity in the Solar Dominion measures their authority against his noon judgment. Khemet's dawn renewal feeds his radiance. Sutekh's chaos exists because Aten-Ra needed something to put on the scale. Even Amunet's hidden power is the shadow his light casts. He is the axis the faction orbits, and the weight that keeps their law from becoming mere brightness.

chapters.title: Gate Wound
chapters.text: The Mythos Gate did not attack Aten-Ra with force. It attacked him with silence — the one thing his noon judgment cannot weigh. When the Hollow leaked through the threshold, it erased the names of warriors who had stood beside him, and Aten-Ra could not remember who they were. His sun-disc heart still radiated, but the light fell on empty space where names should have been. This wound taught him that judgment without memory is not justice — it is merely procedure applied to ghosts.

chapters.title: Campaign Role
chapters.text: In The First Reopening, Aten-Ra anchors the noon judgment against the Hollow's calm erasure. He is the Deity who forces the Gate to answer for what it has taken. His presence on the battlefield means chaos must declare its weight before it can move — but the Hollow's silence is the one weight his scales cannot measure. The campaign tests whether solar authority can judge what it cannot see.

chapters.title: Personal Conflict
chapters.text: Aten-Ra's flaw is certainty. He believes that if law is applied correctly, all things resolve. The Hollow teaches him that some things do not resolve — they simply vanish. His conflict is not with enemies but with the possibility that his own judgment, applied perfectly, could erase a name the Realm needs to survive. The sun that reveals all things may also be the sun that burns what it illuminates.
